kurz: Heat makes the protein strands in meat curl up. Up to about 60 °C it stays juicy; above that the fibres squeeze out more and more juice.
bild_im_kopf: Like wringing out a wet towel: twisted lightly it stays damp, twisted hard everything drips out.
was_passiert: Muscle fibres are made of long protein strands. From about 50 °C the first protein changes; the meat goes from raw to cooked but stays tender. Between about 66 and 73 °C a second protein contracts strongly, the fibres firm up and squeeze out a lot of juice. That is why the [[saftig|juicy]] window for quick-cooked cuts lies roughly between 50 and 60 °C [[kerntemperatur|core temperature]].
warum_wichtig: Explains why a few degrees make the difference between juicy and dry, and why a thermometer helps so much.
faustregeln: Quick-cooked beef: pink at about 54–57 °C core [[temperatur|temperature]], as a guide.
Take it off before it reaches the target: [[nachgaren|carry-over cooking]] adds a few more degrees.
Lean meat is less forgiving than fatty meat.
typische_fehler: Cooking by feel and only stopping once there is no pink left.

praxis.text: Steak and fillet in the window around 55 °C. Pork fillet about 60–63 °C, as a guide.
Fish is even more delicate: it firms up from about 50 °C and falls apart with too much heat.
Egg is protein too: the white sets earlier than the yolk, which is why soft-boiled eggs have a runny yolk.

skala.name: fibres squeeze out a lot of juice
